extracted.intended_audience: literary scholars, narratologists, and advanced creative-writing students interested in narrative technique
extracted.subtask_description: A theoretical framework for analyzing or designing narrative fiction, covering temporal organization, duration, frequency, mood (showing/telling and speech), focalization/perspective, voice (narrating instance and narrative levels), tense/tempo, and related devices. Useful for critics, theorists, and writers aiming to understand or manipulate narrative form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order (chronological organization / anachrony)
rubrics_metrics.description: How events are ordered relative to their telling; includes the manipulation of chronological sequence (anachrony) as a narrational device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses anachrony in classical works (Iliad) and modern novels (Jean Santeuil, Proust). Considers effects of temporal displacements on narrative level and psychology, their frequency/quantity in a text, and how they can function as iteration or scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analepsis (flashback / recall / retrospection)
rubrics_metrics.description: A return in the narrative to events that precede the current narrative point (defined, with reach and extent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes external/internal/mixed and heterodiegetic/homodiegetic analepses; treats completing (returns) vs repeating (recalls); notes traditional functions (revealing ellipsis, resolving enigma) and relations to summary and metadiegetic narration; partial vs complete analepses and their narrative effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prolepsis (flashforward / advance notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advance mention of events that will occur later in the story (defined; organization of narrative by prolepsis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers external and internal prolepses, heterodiegetic/homodiegetic prolepsis, completing vs repeating prolepses, iterative prolepses, and rhetorical uses (advance notice, snares, advance mention), as well as effects like narrative impatience/nostalgia and interactions with focalization and narrating place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration (scene/summary/pause/ellipsis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation between narrated time and discourse time: how long an event is allowed to 'take' in the narrative (defined; includes isochrony).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes scene (slow motion), summary, descriptive pause/description, and ellipsis; discusses boundaries of description, intrusions of narrator, iterative vs singulative duration, and implications for rhythm of classical vs modern novels (with extensive Proustian examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene as duration unit
rubrics_metrics.description: A mode of duration where narrated time is rendered in detail (slow motion), dominating 'showing'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked to dramatic model and 'showing' effect; dominant in scenes and central to classical novel rhythm; in Proust scene interacts with iterative prolepsis and narrative impatience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary as duration unit
rubrics_metrics.description: Condensing larger spans of narrated time into briefer discourse time ('telling').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions as substitute for iterative passages in some contexts; contrasted with scene; important in classical novel rhythm and in handling analepsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipsis (omission of narrated time)
rubrics_metrics.description: A skip over a portion of narrated time (defined; iterative ellipses recognized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ellipses can be revealed by analepsis; iterative ellipses play roles in rhythm and transitions; confusion possible with accelerative devices; Proustian handling emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency (repetition patterns: singulative/iterative/pseudo-iterative)
rubrics_metrics.description: How many times an event is narrated relative to how many times it occurs; includes definitions of repetition and frequency categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines iterative, singulative, pseudo-iterative, repeating narrative; addresses internal/external diachrony, determination/specification/extension/diversification within iterative passages, law of the iterative, and how frequency interrelates with order and duration (notably in Proust).

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative (frequentative narration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narration of events that occur repeatedly; can be internal (synthesizing) or external (generalizing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses frequentative locutions, diversification techniques, internal determination and specification, extension, diachrony, law of frequency, rhythm, transitions to singulative, and Proustian examples (iteratism, intoxication with iteration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Singulative (single-event narration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narration that presents an event as occurring once (singulative); often alternates with iterative passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores contamination by iterative passages in Proust, roles within iterative sections, alternation patterns, and transitions between singulative and iterative modes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pseudo-iterative
rubrics_metrics.description: A form resembling iteration though not strictly iterative (defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Found in classical narrative and in Proust; used as a diversification technique and contrasted with true iteration and pseudo-diegetic devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeating narrative (advance notice / recall / repetition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative operations that repeat material either forward (advance notice) or backward (recall), producing structural reiteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes repeating analepses and prolepses; linked to frequency and order; can produce snares and enigma, and affects focalization and reader expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood (showing vs telling; mimesis vs diegesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation between narrated events and their representation; comprises 'distance' (showing/telling) and 'narrative of words' (speech representation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines mood, distinguishes diegesis and mimesis, treats showing (transparent narrator) vs telling, and situates modes in Proust and classical/modern novels; includes narrative of events and of words as subdomains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood — distance (narrative of events: showing/telling)
rubrics_metrics.description: How narratorial distance shapes presentation of events — 'showing' (mimetic, scene) versus 'telling' (diegetic, summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing tends to make the narrator transparent; telling organizes summary, ellipsis, and description; diegesis/mimesis distinction and its implications for realism and narrative effect are discussed (with Proustian contrasts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mood — narrative of words (speech representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: How speech is represented in the narrative: immediate speech, reported speech, free indirect style, transposed or narrativized speech, interior monologue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers inner speech, objectivization of speech, reported vs immediate speech, free indirect style (link to focalization), narrative of words in modern novel and Proust, and how these modes interact with narrative level and time of narrating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interior monologue / inner speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Representation of a character's inner verbalized thought (defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses definitions and distinctions (Dujardin, Joyce), relation to time of narrating and narrative level, and presence in modernist texts; links to free indirect style and focalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free indirect style
rubrics_metrics.description: A mode blending narrator's voice and a character's speech/thought (defined under narrative of words).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Related to indices of focalization, modalizing locutions, and unavowed paralepsis; key device for internal focalization and de-personalization in modern narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focalization / Perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: The point-of-view through which events are perceived and presented (internal vs external focalization, indices, code of focalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes alterations, polymodality, double focalization, indices and modalizing locutions, concurrent codes, depersonalization, risk and uses of focalization, and its relations to free indirect style, prolepsis/analepsis, and information distribution between hero and narrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paralepsis (unacknowledged omission / selective focalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: A focalization operation where something relevant is unavowedly omitted or left to implication (defined).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as decisive criterion in focalization discussions; covers unavowed paralepsis, its occurrence in Proust, and interactions with paralipsis and indices of focalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paralipsis (deliberate omission and hinting)
rubrics_metrics.description: An explicit or deliberate omission that calls attention to what is omitted (defined; linked to completing analepses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussed alongside paralepsis and analepsis; in Proustous contexts paralipsis interacts with recalls and revealing of ellipses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice (narrating instance / narrative voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence and enunciative position of the narrator (definition of voice, distinction from point of view).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers narrating instance, its place and time, its possible obliteration in modern novels, its relation to immediate speech, and distinction from the writing itself; shows that voice is not invariant and relates to narrating place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrating instance (who tells / enunciating)
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific enunciator in the text (defined), responsible for the act of narrating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses position, place, and time of the narrating instance; its relation to prolepsis; how modern narrative may obscure it; and effects of interpolated narrating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative level (extradeigetic / diegetic / metadiegetic / pseudo-diegetic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Levels of narrative embedding: extradiegetic (outer narrator), diegetic/intradiegetic (narrated narrator), metadiegetic (second-degree narrative), and reduced/pseudo variants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines each level, treats metadiegetic narratives and their functions, reduced metadiegetic/pseudo-diegetic forms, and how analepsis/metalepsis interact with level transitions; discusses Proustian uses and reader effects (trouble from metalepsis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Person (narrative person: homodiegetic/heterodiegetic/autodiegetic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The grammatical/ontological status of the narrator relative to the story (first-person narrator inside or outside the story; autodiegetic = narrator is protagonist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines homodiegetic vs heterodiegetic vs autodiegetic; notes first-person narrator may not equal hero; examines shifts in person and relations to focalization and narrator functions (with many Proustian and Balzacian examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of the narrating (temporal relation of telling to events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the narration is prior (subsequent/retrospective), simultaneous, or subsequent/predictive relative to the narrated events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers prior narrating, predictive narrative, simultaneous narrating, interpolated narrating, and how time of narrating affects focalization, tense, and narrative level; includes Proustian analysis of time of narrating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metalepsis (transgression between narrative levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: A crossing or transgression between narrative levels (defined), producing effects on status and reader reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses metalepsis as problematic (troubling the reader), links to analepsis and metadiegetic narrative, mentions metalepsis examples and how it affects the status of the narrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing vs Telling (mimesis vs diegesis)
rubrics_metrics.description: A core stylistic/evaluative distinction: 'showing' (mimetic, scene-based, transparent narrator) versus 'telling' (diegetic, summary-based).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a criterion for narrative realism and immediacy; 'showing' correlates with scene and immediate speech while 'telling' correlates with summary, commentary, and narrator intrusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative information and information distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: How information is allocated between narrator, hero, and reader; includes indices and realistic motivation for information presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines information of hero vs narrator, indices of focalization, the implied reader, and narrative competence; discusses realistic motivation and how information handling shapes reader interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrator functions (pragmatic roles of the narrator)
rubrics_metrics.description: The various roles a narrator can perform (commentary, intrusions, ideological function, guiding the implied reader, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists functions such as descriptive intrusions, guidance to reader, speculative/explanatory discourse, and ideological functions; cites functions enumerated in the text (e.g., functions of the narrator, 255-259) with examples from Balzac, Stendhal, Sterne.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implied reader / narrative competence
rubrics_metrics.description: The presupposed reader for whom the narrative is organized and who has the narrative competence to decode codes and snares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses the implied reader as distinct from the actual recipient, the reader's narrative competence (deciphering codes, enigma resolution), and the implied reader's relation to Proustian narrative and Balzacian description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic motivation / realistic effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether narrative devices (temporal distortions, focalization choices) have plausible motivations within the story world and produce a realistic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes realistic motivation that justifies temporal/focal choices, links realistic effect with mimesis, and considers how devices might be seen as realistic or as deliberate formal manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tempo / Rhythm / Speed
rubrics_metrics.description: How narrative speed and rhythm are measured and manipulated (relation of narrated to discourse time; musical metaphors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses measurement of speed, rhythm of classical narrative, musical treatment of temporality (Proust), and how tempo interacts with duration, frequency, and realistic motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description (descriptive pause)
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative passages devoted to description, often experienced as pauses in action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines descriptive pause and boundaries, its role in duration, relations to focalization and mimesis, and Balzacian/Bloomfield examples of description shaping reader's interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embeddings / narrative embeddings / narrative level transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Structures where one narrative is embedded within another (frame stories, metadiegetic embeddings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explores embeddings' impact on narrative level, metalepsis risk, reader confusion, and narrative organization (e.g., frame stories, second-degree narratives, pseudo-diegetic forms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enigma / Suspense
rubrics_metrics.description: Devices that create questions or mysteries to be resolved by the narrative (enigma; snares).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects enigma to prolepsis/analepsis, repeating narratives, and narrative suspense; mentions Barthes' enigma and snares and their role in reader engagement and narrative pacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative license
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorial freedom to manipulate temporal, focal, and voice devices beyond mimetic realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as a concept that allows transgressions of classical norms (e.g., iterative practices, anachrony) while still producing literary effects; must be considered relative to reader expectations and realistic motivation.
